mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined in 3 of the last 4 weeks (-39.9 to -40.9) with no reversal signal, indicating persistent momentum that will continue to suppress retail footfall over the next four weeks absent a shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -39.9 to -40.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days, reversing the observed momentum.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility above 9.0 signals increased risk-averse sheltering behavior, which within two weeks translates into reduced discretionary retail and recreation visits.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 8.7 to 9.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the following two weeks despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 9.0.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent four-week decline in WORKPLACES (-45.1 to -46.1) reflects renewed office-closure or remote-work policy responses during a Delta-variant surge, which depresses adjacent lunchtime and after-work retail activity for the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined from -45.1 to -46.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even as WORKPLACES continues to decline, indicating decoupling from workplace policy effects.

mechanism_narrative: Joint declines in TRANSIT (-37.4 to -39.0) and WORKPLACES (-45.1 to -46.1) interact to compound reductions in combined commute-linked retail visits, producing a sharper RETAIL_REC decline than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES declined over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline magnitude does not exceed the decline predicted by TRANSIT or WORKPLACES individually, indicating no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PARKS mobility (-0.3 to -3.4 in the latest week) signals reduced outdoor leisure activity, likely due to late-summer weather shifts or caution, which shifts some recreation demand away from retail-adjacent outdoor venues within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell sharply from -0.3 to -3.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week immediately following a PARKS decline of this magnitude.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stayed in a narrow band (-16.6 to -17.9) over four weeks, indicating a stable essential-shopping-only behavioral pattern that will persist and keep non-essential RETAIL_REC suppressed at similarly low levels over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fluctuated within a narrow -16.6 to -17.9 range
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises substantially while GROCERY_PHARM remains flat, indicating decoupling of essential vs discretionary shopping behavior.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls more than 2 additional points week-on-week beyond the current -39.0, it signals an escalating mobility-restriction regime (e.g., renewed capacity limits or advisories) that will rapidly depress RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 2 points week-on-week below -39.0
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declined from -37.4 to -39.0 over the snapshot period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within one week of a TRANSIT drop exceeding 2 points, indicating the trigger threshold is not predictive.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous rise in RESIDENTIAL (8.7 to 9.3) and decline in WORKPLACES (-45.1 to -46.1) jointly indicate a reinforcing stay-at-home shift where reduced commuting and increased home-dwelling interact to compound suppression of retail trips over four weeks beyond what either series predicts alone.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose while WORKPLACES fell concurrently over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline is no greater than what RESIDENTIAL or WORKPLACES alone would predict, indicating no interaction effect between the two drivers.
